decisions.summary: clip_to_clear decides with fabric_index(obstacles, margin, (), 0.0, lines, line_margin).fouled
decisions.why: FR-001 verbatim: the closure is fouled_brute term for term, and FabricIndex.fouled equals fouled_brute (feature 138/145 oracle); fabric_index is the memoized path clear_runs already asks, as FR-001 names.

decisions.summary: a module store of RingIndex keyed by the ring's points, cleared in clearance.reset(), bounded at 4,096 and cleared whole
decisions.why: FR-002: content key, cleared with _MEMO in reset() at roll end; the bound only forces rebuilds, never a stale reuse.

decisions.summary: toll grid cells of max(20, radius + 1), 3x3 read, same math.dist <= r
decisions.why: FR-003 as written; a cell strictly larger than the radius keeps 'at most one cell away' true in floating point at an exact boundary, so the 3x3 read is a superset and the same test decides.

decisions.summary: outermost_join asks seg_reach_index widened by reach + 1e-6; RouteReach files route points in a PointGrid; routes_missed kept as a one-shot wrapper; one RouteReach per candidate loop in siting.py and frame.py
decisions.why: FR-004: both indexes prune, the same closed tests decide; any/count are order-free.

decisions.summary: _link_home_bank files the brook's segments once in a PointGrid by box; crossing and parity tests ask the segments whose box meets
decisions.why: FR-005 first half: a segment index; segments whose boxes do not meet cannot cross, so crossing counts and parity are unchanged.

decisions.summary: the stream segments filed once in a PointGrid by box widened by each segment's hw and cached; the cache holds the streams list, each record and each course and compares them by identity with each course's length and width (not _water_obstacles' length key); a rect asks near(center, half its extent) and the old seg_dist < hw / segments_cross decide; lifted to rect_touches_stream
decisions.why: FR-005 second half as written: a segment index of the watercourse built once and asked per rect. Round 3: the restated key is strictly stronger than the length key it replaces (a same-length list swap, the feature-261 case, now rebuilds); as built in fit.py _rect_on_stream it compares list identity, count, record and course identity, length and w, and stream_segment_index uses the same hw (w/2 + 5, default 9) as _water_obstacles. The residual exposure (a course mutated in place at the same length) is stated and matches clearance._MEMO's; PointGrid.near is a square query that never omits a box within pad, so the same closed tests decide. Research R2 reports the pool byte-identical against c13a6ebe6. Exactness serves 'without any loss in accuracy'; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: lane_seat_index filed by raw box with max half; probe asks near(cx, cy, maxhalf + boxhalf) and the same strict seg_dist test; built once in place_kosatsuba's loop and once per clear_label_seat call
decisions.why: FR-006: a Chebyshev-padded grid query is a superset of the Euclidean test; the lanes do not change within those probe runs.

decisions.summary: edge_m memo keyed (fv, j, n) used only after rspan is live; the f_hi probe keeps calling edge
decisions.why: FR-007 first half exactly; edge reads only fixed closure state (phase, rphase, rowamp, rspan once live, sup_idx) and pure helpers (_bnd, _clear_supply), no random draw.

decisions.summary: a gap (pa, pb) that took no seat is recorded and skipped in later rounds; GroveBlocks.static_clear memoized per point for the gap fill only
decisions.why: FR-008: GroveBlocks, within, _near and _wv are fixed through the fill; only near_seats grows, so a barren gap's identical candidates stay refused; skipping it has no side effect on other gaps; the boolean chain is preserved.

decisions.summary: _quad_in_supply memoizes each edge's verdict per carve under the unordered endpoint pair, walked lesser-to-greater
decisions.why: FR-007 second half and its accepted Decisions row; held to SC-011's moving condition.

decisions.summary: WITHDRAWN (spec Amendment 1): the vectorized marsh was built and measured and is removed; the marsh keeps its scalar throws
decisions.why: Narrows the accepted spec (FR-009, SC-010), not the GM's words: the request asks to 'see what we could do to improve it' - performance - and never names the marsh. Keeping B2 would defeat the request's stated purpose concretely: research R2 measured the hinterland stage flat on four maps and slower on Kuwabata (0.380 -> 0.443 s, observed 2026-09-28, fastest of three), while moving every map's marsh marks - a map change bought for no speed. This is not a session completing the GM's thought; it is the measurement the request itself asks for ('take a set of measurements and see what's slow') ruling a lever out. Contingent on Amendment 1's parallel spec review: if that review rejects the withdrawal, this decision is reopened. Round 4: the plan's summary, Constitution Check XII, the SC-010 row, the C ordering and the verification table now all mark B2 withdrawn; no passage still reads as if it lands.

decisions.summary: the marsh's pond-bank keep-out files each fish-pond bank's WHOLE ring in the KeepoutGrid (slot 2) instead of every 16th point, so a reed cannot stand in a drawn corner the thinned chord cut; kept when B2 was withdrawn; tested by test_a_pond_bank_keeps_the_reeds_off_the_same_way
decisions.why: Read wet.py line 313: _banks now takes dp['bank'] whole (the diff from c13a6ebe6 removes only the [:: len//16] stride), filed by keep.rings(_banks, slot=2, reach=max(_pads)) exactly as before. This is the request's own invariant stated verbatim - 'as long as things that aren't supposed to overlap don't overlap' - enforced where a reed based inside the bank's drawn corner passed; and constitution XIV (fix where found). It adds no new rule (reeds off planted earth is feature 150 T54's existing rule) and narrows nothing; the spec carries it in Decisions Recorded (historically accurate, the existing rule now enforced at the drawn corners). The pool is reported byte-identical, so no drawn map moved.

decisions.summary: the committed pool at c13a6ebe6 first confirmed to regenerate byte-identically in the base worktree; A1-A8 land and the pool is diffed against it (or a merged commit's own confirmed regeneration after a sync-in); then B1 (and B2 until its withdrawal, B3 with it) under 276's FR-006 condition
decisions.why: SC-011 as written; confirming the reference regenerates at the base makes the byte-identity diff a test of A1-A8 rather than of drift, and the sync-in fallback confirms its reference the same way. Round 4: the ordering now records B2's withdrawal and B3 riding with B1; the spec's Amendment 1 reports the landed pool byte-identical against c13a6ebe6.

decisions.summary: SC-002 to SC-010 counted by a sys.monitoring entry-bucket instrument in harness.py: every call beneath a mechanism's entry functions (new builders included) credited to its bucket, innermost entry exclusive; each bucket's total recorded beside its named count; same harness in base and clone; base-rerun over after, differences from the before-* figures reported
decisions.why: Answers round 1: the moved calls (RingIndex under FabricIndex.fouled, the ring store under FabricIndex.__init__, RouteReach, the stream and lane indexes) are beneath the listed entries, so they are counted wherever they move, and a named count that falls while its bucket's total does not is ruled a finding, not a pass. The counted callees match the SCs' named quantities (seg_dist, RingIndex builds, dict.get for the toll's cell lookups as counts.py took them, segments_cross, edge, GroveBlocks tests, KeepoutGrid.hit). Measures what the SCs name; narrows nothing.
